'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]], [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that the [[United States]] will end their support for [[Saudi Arabia]] in their intervention in [[Yemen]]. However, he also said the United States will continue targeting [[al-Qaeda]] operations in the country. [https://www.ft.com/content/b592364d-080e-4e30-a3dd-5910c0a12146 (''The Financial Times'')]
*[[Lebanon|Lebanese]] political activist and [[Hezbollah]] critic [[Lokman Slim]] is [[assassinate]]d, with his body being found inside his car with multiple gunshot wounds in [[Sidon District]]. [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Hassan Diab]] says "this heinous crime shall not pass without accountability". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-55933222 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[New Zealand]] announces a new floating [[Public holidays in New Zealand|public holiday]] to commence in 2022 based on the [[Māori culture|Māori]] celebration of [[Matariki]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/435789/prime-minister-jacinda-ardern-reveals-date-of-first-matariki-public-holiday (RNZ)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Wooroloo bushfire]]
**The number of homes destroyed rises to 81, as a new [[bushfire]] to the north threatens the [[Bullsbrook, Western Australia|Bullsbrook]] township. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-04/number-of-homes-lost-in-perth-hills-bushfire-revised-up-to-81/13117488 (ABC Australia)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
*****[[Governor of Wisconsin|Governor]] [[Tony Evers]] issues a new [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] after the [[Wisconsin Legislature|Legislature]] voted to repeal the original mandate. [https://apnews.com/article/wisconsin-governor-mask-mandate-d8436b7f9a7539e9d1cd2589483916d8 (AP)]
****President of the 75th session of the [[United Nations General Assembly]] [[Volkan Bozkır]] receives his first dose of [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/un-general-assembly-president-volkan-bozkir-receives-covid-19-vaccine-121020500061_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
****[[Johnson & Johnson]] requests emergency approval for its vaccine from the [[Food and Drug Administration]]. [https://www.cnet.com/health/johnson-johnson-seeks-fda-emergency-authorization-for-covid-19-vaccine/ (CNET)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] says he is in "good health and recovering" after testing positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in late January. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-mexico-president-idUSL1N2KB09W (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Cambodia)|Ministry of Health]] grants emergency use authorization for China's [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50810677/health-ministry-grants-emergency-use-authorization-to-chinas-sinopharm-vaccine/ (''Khmer Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] receives its first shipment of 500,000 doses of Russia's [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/first-batch-of-russian-covid-19-vaccine-arrives-in-iran/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]]
****[[State of Palestine|Palestine]] receives 10,000 doses of Russia's Sputnik V [[vaccine]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/palestine-gets-10-000-doses-of-russian-covid-19-vaccine/2133792# (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports its first death of a foreigner from [[COVID-19]]. The patient was a British national in his 70s. It is also the first death from the B.1.1.7 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] reported in the country. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4119862 (''Taiwan News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[France]] reports four cases of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in [[Brazil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-france-variant/france-registers-four-cases-of-brazilian-coronavirus-variant-says-minister-idUSP6N2I8010 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] surpasses 90,000 deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.ilmessaggero.it/salute/focus/covid_italia_oggi_bollettino_4_febbraio_2021_contagi_morti_ultima_ora-5745476.html (''Il Messaggero'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[Government of the United Kingdom|government]] confirms that British nationals and non-residents returning from 30 "red list" high-risk countries will need to quarantine in hotels or government-approved accommodation beginning February 15, two weeks after it was announced by [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-mandatory-hotel-quarantine-will-come-into-effect-on-15-february-12208879 (Sky News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Private gatherings in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] are limited to 15 people after a worker at a [[quarantine]] site for [[tennis]] players competing in the [[Australian Open]] tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/feb/03/australian-open-players-and-officials-isolate-after-covid-positive-at-hotel (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
***[[Peru]] signs a deal with [[Pfizer]] to purchase 20 million doses of its [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://gestion.pe/peru/vacunas-covid-19-peru-firma-acuerdo-por-20-millones-de-vacunas-con-pfizer-y-primera-entregas-seran-en-marzo-y-abril-nndc-noticia/?outputType=amp (''Gestión'')]
*[[2019–2021 locust infestation]]
**[[Somalia]] declares a [[state of emergency]] due to swarms of desert [[locust]]s. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/africa/somalia-declares-state-of-emergency-over-locust-swarms (''Daily Sabah'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2020–2021 Indian farmers protest]]
**The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] calls for [[India]] to resolve the [[2020–2021 Indian farmers' protest|farmers' protests]] via dialogue. However, the [[Ministry of External Affairs (India)|Ministry of External Affairs]] compared reactions to the [[2021 Indian farmers' Republic Day protest|January 26th incident]] at [[Red Fort]] to the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riot]] that occurred at the [[United States Capitol|Capitol]]. [https://www.nationalheraldindia.com/national/after-us-remarks-on-farmers-protest-india-compares-reactions-to-red-fort-violence-to-capitol-hill-incident (''National Herald'')]
**A probe by the Modi government to the source of a protest toolkit [[Greta Thunberg]] posted suggested it was put together by a [[Canadian]] [[Khalistan|pro-Khalistan]] organization and that the toolkit had a plan to carry forward the "malign Indian campaign" even if the government repealed the laws. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/farmers-protest-canada-based-pro-khalistani-outfit-blamed-for-organising-twitter-toolkit/articleshow/80695955.cms (''Times of India'')]
*[[Foreign relations of Guyana]], [[Foreign relations of Taiwan]]
**[[Taiwan]] announces that it will establish a [[Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office]] in [[Guyana]]. The [[United States]] welcomes the "milestone". [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/taiwan-opens-trade-office-in-guyana-14110416 (AFP via CNA)]
**After criticism from [[China]], Guyana terminates the above agreement and says it will continue to follow the [[One-China policy]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/04/guyana-taiwan-office-agreement-beijing-criticism (''The Guardian'')]
*[[China–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] broadcasting regulator [[Ofcom]] revokes the license of [[China Global Television Network]] (CGTN), an [[English-language]] Chinese news network, after concluding the network was "ultimately controlled" by the [[Chinese Communist Party]]. China responds to the move by accusing [[BBC News]] of spreading "[[fake news]]" about COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-ofcom-cgtn/uk-regulator-revokes-chinese-tv-licence-beijing-complains-about-bbc-fake-news-idUSKBN2A41KQ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Turkey–United States relations]]
**[[cabinet of Turkey|Turkish]] [[Ministry of the Interior (Turkey)|Interior Minister]] [[Süleyman Soylu]] accuses the [[United States]] of being behind the [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt|coup d'état attempt in 2016]], which killed more than 250 people. The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] says the accusation was "wholly false", and "inconsistent with Turkey's status as a [[NATO]] ally". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-usa/turkish-minister-says-u-s-behind-2016-failed-coup-hurriyet-idUSKBN2A502S?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Henry Puna]] becomes the new Secretary-General of the [[Pacific Islands Forum]] replacing [[Meg Taylor]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/435765/former-cook-islands-pm-is-the-new-secretary-general-of-the-pif (RNZ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Kilmarnock incidents]]
**A woman is stabbed to death outside a hospital, and another killed at a nearby street, in [[Ayrshire]], [[Scotland]]. The perpetrator dies during a car crash while escaping from the scene. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-55948245 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[117th United States Congress]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 230–199 to remove Rep. [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]-[[Georgia (U.S. state)|GA]]) from her assignments on the [[United States House Committee on Education and Labor|Education and Labor]] and [[United States House Committee on the Budget|Budget]] committees. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-55940542 (BBC News)] 

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]], [[Censorship in Myanmar]], [[Censorship of Facebook]]
**American technology company [[Facebook, Inc.]] reports that multiple [[Internet in Myanmar#Service providers|Internet service providers in Myanmar]] have restricted access to its [[social networking service]]s, including [[Facebook]], [[Instagram]], and [[WhatsApp]]. The company has urged authorities to restore connectivity. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/facebook-says-services-in-coup-hit-myanmar-disrupted-947275.html (AFP via ''Deccan Herald'')]
